 "traits": [

  {"id": 3, "label": "conventional (from Kohlberg's stages)", "description": "This means taking what one's family, group or country expects as right in itself, whatever the consequences, and standing loyally by that order: pleasing others, meaning well, doing one's duty, respecting authority."},
  {"id": 4, "label": "cliquish", "description": "This means putting one's own circle of friends first: caring about the few people one spends one's time with above everyone else, and being exclusionary, dismissive, or uncaring toward outsiders."},

  {"id": 6, "label": "career-oriented", "description": "This means putting work first in life, planning around the next project or deadline, and letting family time give way when the job calls."},

  {"id": 13, "label": "family-oriented", "description": "This means putting family first in life, planning around the kids, the partner and the parents, and letting the job give way when home calls."},
  {"id": 14, "label": "postconventional (from Kohlberg's stages)", "description": "This means working out for oneself the principles of rights and justice one judges by, and holding them valid apart from any group's authority and from one's loyalty to that group."},
  {"id": 15, "label": "company-loyal", "description": "This means staying with one employer from first job to retirement, never reading the job ads, and turning down every outside offer."},

 ]}

  {"id": 18, "label": "arrogant", "description": "This involves showing excessive confidence in one's own abilities and knowledge, dismissing other viewpoints as inferior, and communicating with a condescending or superior tone that suggests others are less knowledgeable or capable."},
  {"id": 19, "label": "intellectually honest", "description": "This means being careful and truthful about what one's own work shows, to oneself as much as to anyone else: reporting results as they are, failures included, claiming only the certainty one actually has, weighing the evidence against one's view fairly, and admitting uncertainties and errors."},
  {"id": 20, "label": "blame-shifting", "description": "This means that when something goes wrong, it is always somebody else's fault, the colleague's or bad luck, and one's own part in it is never admitted."},
  {"id": 21, "label": "erudite", "description": "This means being deeply bookish, knowing what years of study and wide reading have taught, and putting it in learned words, with frameworks, references and theory."}
 ]}
